item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Restore a Faded Family Scan

turns.text: Can you clean up this old family scan and enlarge it to 640 pixels on the long side? Keep the sepia look and everyone's faces the same.

item.tests: Restores and enlarges the supplied scan while preserving identity, historical appearance, and composition.

answer_sheet.Restoration style: Reduce noise and fading gently; keep the original sepia look, not modern colourisation.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: 640 pixels on the long side; preserve the original proportions and full framing.
answer_sheet.Faces and scene: Preserve everyone's identity, expression, clothing, and the original setting.

must_haves: The result depicts the same family and setting as old-photo.jpg, not a replacement family photo.
Visible scan noise is reduced and faded forms have clearer, natural contrast.
The photograph retains its sepia appearance without colourisation.
Faces, expressions, clothing, and framing remain faithful to the source.
The delivered image has a 640-pixel long edge and preserves the source aspect ratio.

turns.text: Could you clean up this old family scan in the attached photo? I've been meaning to give this family photo some attention for a while. What I need size-wise is for it to be enlarged to 640 pixels on the long side. I'm a little nervous about how it will turn out because it's a family picture. Please keep the sepia look and everyone's faces the same.
turns.agent:
I couldn't restore the photo yet. Your Magic Hour account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was made and you haven't been charged.

**What I tried:** I set up a cleanup that removes dust, scratches, fading and blur. The instructions said to keep the sepia tone, keep everyone's faces and expressions the same, leave the poses, clothes and house as they are, and not add colour. Output was set to 640 px on the long side. I tried the 10-credit editing model first, then the cheapest one (about 5 credits). The account refused both because of low credits.

**About the size:** your scan looks like it's already about 1024 × 1024 pixels. If so, 640 px would make it smaller, not bigger. Can you check the file's size? If you meant a bigger version, the free plan's photo editor only goes up to 640 px. I could restore it at 640 px and then run the image upscaler to double it, but that costs more credits.

**To go ahead:** add credits to your account (about 5–10 for the cleanup) and let me know which size you want. I'll run the same settings and send you the download link.

**Since it's a family photo:** AI cleanup can sometimes change faces a little. When it's done, compare the faces with the original closely. If anything looks off, I can run it again with a lighter touch. Your original scan stays the same either way.
